comment: Tree definition for mkimage.py. Exactly one source per file entry:
"asset":  bytes from tools/bootlab/assets/<value> (committed)
"file":   bytes from tools/bootlab/<value>, resolved relative to
tools/bootlab (so "../../Libraries/..." leaves the dir)
"kernel": work/stripped_kernel.development if newer than
assets/kernel.development, else the committed asset
"init":   work/init (built by build_init.sh from init/init_static.c)
"init_exec": work/init_exec (dynamic gate PID1, from
init/init_exec_dynamic.c; see manifest_dynamic.json)
"text":   inline string, utf-8
"glob":   directory passthrough: every regular file under
assets/<asset_prefix> lands at <path>/<filename>
Paths are case-insensitive on FAT; canonical names here are lowercase.
P1 (2026-10-02) -- THIS FILE NO LONGER GLOBS.  It used to carry
{ "glob": "usr/lib/system", "asset_prefix": "usr/lib/system/" },
which staged all 46 files in that directory: 31 of them extracted from
the host Mac's dyld shared cache, 28 of them rejected by dyld2's LINKEDIT
validation, and the whole tree failing closure with 84 unresolved
non-weak undefined symbols and 3 unstaged dependencies.  The 31
host-extracted binaries have since been MOVED out of assets/ into
tools/bootlab/assets-quarantine/ -- see
assets-quarantine/QUARANTINE_INVENTORY.txt for every sha256, filetype and
milestone identity.  So the glob is not merely unnecessary now, it is
unresolvable: mkimage would fail on a missing prefix.  The closure is
named entry by entry, exactly as in manifest_cpmv.json, and every
"asset:" entry below is either a plist or a text file -- there is no
Apple binary under assets/ any more.
WHAT IS STILL AN assets/ BYTE, AND WHY IT IS ALLOWED:
assets/com.apple.Boot.plist  a text plist the firmware reads
assets/etc/rc                the historical rc stub (dead path;
README records the program is not in
the tree)
assets/hello.txt             a text file
assets/BOOTX64.EFI, boot.efi, kernel.development, vars.fd
non-binary/loader or kernel payloads,
and every one of them is superseded:
both EFI paths here are the source-built
apple-free loader from work/efi/.
assets/usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib  a build product of Libraries/objc4
(byte-identical to ../../Libraries/
objc4/libobjc.A.dylib), staged here for
stage_dynamic_libs.sh.  NOT quarantined,
NOT host-extracted.  The closure below
names the repo path directly, so this
copy is not staged by this manifest.
VERIFIED, 2026-10-02:
python3 closure_gate.py manifest.json   -> PASS, HOST-EXTRACTED 0
python3 provenance_scan.py --target assets -> HOST-EXTRACTED 0
